channel.title: ShopNow Kitchen
channel.description: Basket or oven-style? Compare before you buy. Specs, sources and the questions that decide it — no hype.

item.title: What does ±0.5°F actually mean? Check your thermometer at home in three minutes
item.description: A listing can claim half a degree. Federal guidance says most food thermometers read accurate within 2 to 4 degrees. Here is the 30-second ice test that tells you which one you own.

item.title: Will it fit? Four measurements to take before an air fryer arrives
item.description: One listing says 13.4 inches deep, another says 16.9 inches and 26.5 pounds. Take these four measurements first — the returns desk is not a plan.

item.title: Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?
item.description: Two baskets that finish together vs. one big oven cavity. Compare capacity, footprint, and cleanup across the three air fryers in the shop.

item.title: Your first air fryer: the six checks before you buy
item.description: Buying your first air fryer? Six checks that come straight off the listing — capacity, footprint, weight, temperature range, power, dishwasher-safe parts — so you do not regret it in a month.

item.title: Reheating holiday leftovers in an air fryer: the food-safety rules that matter
item.description: Two hours, four days, 165°F: the USDA numbers that decide whether tomorrow's plate is worth reheating — and where an air fryer fits, and where it does not.

item.title: Instant-read or leave-in probe: which one actually does your job?
item.description: One thermometer you spot-check with, and one that stays in the food and tells you when to stop. The difference is not luxury — it is what you can walk away from.

item.title: Air fryer vs. convection oven: what actually changes?
item.description: Air fryer, convection oven, toaster oven — the names overlap. Here is what each listing in the shop actually says it does, and the one question that decides which shape you need.

item.title: How much food actually fits in 6 quarts?
item.description: Quarts are a volume, not a serving count. Here is what the listings in the shop actually state about capacity, and the honest answer to how much food a 6-quart basket really holds.

item.title: How to read an air fryer listing: which specs to compare and which words to skip
item.description: Capacity shape, temperature range, wattage, footprint, weight, cleanup: the six fields worth comparing across the three air fryers in the shop — and the marketing words that carry no information.

item.title: A no-hype checklist for comparing air fryer capacity
item.description: Quarts mean different things. Measure the food, not the marketing — a practical capacity checklist for the three air fryers in the shop.

item.title: Cooking for a crowd this season: four thermometer questions to settle before Thursday
item.description: A bird, a roast and four hours of oven. What to decide about probes, alarms, and cable heat limits before you buy anything for the holiday cook.

item.title: How to assess cleanup and counter-space trade-offs
item.description: Dishwasher-safe parts, windows, and the inches your counter actually has. A practical cleanup and footprint guide for basket vs. oven-style fryers.

item.title: Questions to ask before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance
item.description: 24 functions sound great — until you ask which ones you will use weekly. Questions for oven-style fryers and wireless thermometers.

item.title: Cooking a turkey this week: where does the probe actually go?
item.description: USDA gives the number (165°F for all poultry) and the three places to check it. Which thermometer style gets you that reading — and where each one goes — decides the rest.

item.title: Black Friday air fryer deals: what should you check before you click buy?
item.description: A pre-click checklist for deal season: which size is on the page, what the listing contradicts about itself, and why this site shows no deal price at all.
